unmapped_findings: Alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al (4 wt.% Al addition) is an intermediate variant of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP set; the 4 wt.% Al addition is explicitly reported among the intermediate variants. [b0019, b0024, b0025]
For Al content below 5 wt.%, a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature; this 4 wt.% Al sample therefore belongs to the single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel class. [b0015, b0031]

Compositions with 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al show the TWIP effect as the prevailing deformation mechanism (dislocation-based strain hardening followed by mechanical twinning at higher loads). [b0031]

Alloys with 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% Al additions are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening). [b0024]
Intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al show a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior than the ~8 wt.% Al variant. [b0025]

Al promotes the formation of nanoprecipitates upon aging with L'12 (L′1₂) structure and approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)3AlC (referred to as κ-carbides); these have a lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to an austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix (this is a general statement, not specifically quantified for the 450 °C/1 h condition). [b0015]

This sample was synthesized within the rapid alloy prototyping (RAP) combinatorial approach for trend screening and alloy maturation of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density TWIP and κ-carbide hardened steels. [b0019]
